answer: Peer-prediction grading: each grader scores an answer and also predicts how other graders will score it, and pay follows a truth-serum rule that rewards honest reports that turn out surprisingly common. A sybil ring that rubber-stamps its own answers has to bet against the real crowd and keeps losing its stake. Like an atlas that marks every false oasis, the rule maps collusion; each fake quill must stake real tokens, so a ring of a thousand bleeds a thousand stakes.
